transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2027-09-01
Start: 15:00 UTC
Duration: ~45 minutes
Attendees: Dana Rivera (Redwood AE), Kofi Mensah (Redwood SE), Aisha Patel (Head of ML, Cormorant), Marco Ruiz (CTO), Olivia Chen (Security)

Summary (auto-generated, may be imperfect): quick discovery to understand model selection needs for multi-lingual customer-facing assistants, context-length requirements (long docs / 100k tokens), and hosted vs dedicated vs private deployment trade-offs; security -> VPC/KMS and audit logs called out. Next steps: pricing, benchmarks, security docs.

Transcript:
[00:00] Dana Rivera: hey everyone, thanks for joining, um yeah I'll kick us off. This is Dana from Redwood, with Kofi who's our SE. How are you all doing?
[00:06] Aisha Patel: good, thanks, sorry slight delay — got pulled into another call but we're here.
[00:09] Marco Ruiz: hi, Marco here. quick context from our side: Cormorant's building a multi-lingual support assistant that needs to read long policy docs and tool-call into our ticketing system. so model selection is kinda central — latency and cost matter.
[00:21] Kofi Mensah: great, thanks Marco. can you confirm rough qps and typical context sizes? you mentioned long docs, is that like 8k? 32k? 100k?
[00:30] Aisha Patel: yes, so a mix — most interactions are short but we have an ingestion pipeline where the assistant must consider full policy PDFs, sometimes up to 70-90k tokens for batch summarization, and for certain workflows we need 100k+ context. we're also supporting Spanish, Portuguese, and Japanese, so multilingual is key.
[00:46] Dana Rivera: okay that's super helpful. couple of dimensions we'll talk about: model choice (open LLMs vs Redwood-verified variants), deployment mode (hosted, dedicated, private/VPC), tool-calling/function calling support, and perf/cost tradeoffs.
[00:56] Marco Ruiz: on tool-calling, we need to call our ticketing API and a discovery vector DB — ideally function-calling or a structured tool invocation. any limitations there?
[01:05] Kofi Mensah: we support function-calling patterns and structured tool outputs; our hosted API supports streaming and tool responses. for private deployments it's the same runtime but you bring networking constraints. small caveat: some older open model variants might not have built-in tool-call hooks out of the box, so we pair them with a thin shim.
[01:18] Olivia Chen: from security POV we need SOC2 type II, SSO (SAML), audit logs and customer-managed KMS. what's available across hosting options?
[01:26] Dana Rivera: hosted API includes SOC2 attestation, SSO for team access, and audit logs in the console. for customer-managed KMS and strict network isolation, Dedicated and Private (VPC/on-prem) are your options — Private gives you the control plane in your VPC and KMS integration. we'll send the security pack with certs.
[01:40] Aisha Patel: good. also curious about quantization and performance — if we go for 100k context, what's realistic latency and cost?
[01:47] Kofi Mensah: okay so large context changes the math. for 100k tokens we typically recommend models with efficient attention or segmented retrieval + KV cache. latency depends on model family and hardware — on dedicated A100/H100 configs you can get inference for long contexts in the 1.5-5s range for single-shot summarization workloads, but if you need real-time chat with 100k prefix, it's heavier. cost per token will be higher; we usually recommend a hybrid: compress/segment the doc and use retrieval augmented generation to reduce active context, or run batch summarization jobs on Dedicated.
[02:12] Marco Ruiz: hmm, so a mix of retrieval + shorter working context might be the approach. do you have recommended open models for multi-lingual + long context?
[02:21] Kofi Mensah: yes — beyond the obvious, there are some open families like Mistral/Orca derivatives, and newer long-context variants — eg LlamaX-long, Mosaic-long, but names get fuzzy. Redwood maintains a catalog with verified performance profiles; we'll point you to models we benchmarked for multi-lingual QA and 100k context. some models are quantization-friendly which helps on Dedicated.
[02:39] Aisha Patel: and embeddings — we need multi-lingual dense vectors; any limitations?
[02:43] Dana Rivera: hosted embeddings are multi-lingual; we also provide recommendations on which model to use per language. for on-prem some older models need extra steps.
[02:50] Olivia Chen: about data residency — we're in EMEA with EU-only data residency requirements. can Hosted comply?
[02:55] Dana Rivera: yes, we have EU regions and can pin processing to EU. Dedicated and Private of course stay in customer region. we'll note that in the security doc.
[03:02] Marco Ruiz: latency SLOs — if we go hosted, can we get SLOs?
[03:06] Dana Rivera: hosted has best-effort SLAs; Dedicated comes with SLA-backed uptime and latency targets for reserved capacity. Private is negotiated. Many customers start hosted then move to Dedicated once steady throughput justifies it.
[03:15] Aisha Patel: can you run a POC bench where we push our 100k documents and measure throughput?
[03:19] Kofi Mensah: absolutely. typical POC plan: 1) upload test corpus + sample prompts, 2) run benchmark with several model variants and precisions (fp16/int8), 3) compare latency/cost and quality. we can do that in hosted or a temporary Dedicated pool.
[03:31] Olivia Chen: on auditability: do logs include per-token tracing or just request/response?
[03:35] Kofi Mensah: the console gives request/response traces, token counts, latency; we can turn on detailed tracing for POC. for Private we can stream logs to your SIEM.
[03:43] Marco Ruiz: OK. budget question — roughly how much for a pilot that runs 100k-doc summarizations for 10k docs?
[03:49] Dana Rivera: rough ballpark depends on model and config; we'll send a pilot pricing page. my quick guess: low tens of thousands for a month if using Dedicated reserved burst capacity; hosted can be higher per-token but no infra commit. we'll provide the matrix.
[04:01] Aisha Patel: got it. can you talk about fallbacks — if the primary model is down or capacity constrained?
[04:06] Kofi Mensah: we support smart routing and fallback to compatible model variants or lower-precision configs. you can define routing policies by latency, cost, and region. Redwood will failover automatically based on policy. small note: when you fallback model families, outputs may shift, so we recommend guardrails and evals tied to prompt sets.
[04:23] Marco Ruiz: good catch. for tool-calling specifically we need guaranteed structured outputs for our ticketing API — JSON with specific fields — how reliable is that?
[04:31] Kofi Mensah: fairly reliable when you use function-calling schemas and few-shot examples. some open models vary; our SDK has validation hooks to enforce schema and reject non-conforming responses. we recommend a small post-processor layer for critical workflows.
[04:44] Aisha Patel: about model updates/versioning — we want reproducible outputs for compliance. can we pin versions?
[04:48] Dana Rivera: yes, you can pin model versions and roll out canary or A/B tests via the Console. Redwood tracks model versions and you can lock a route to a version.
[04:56] Olivia Chen: SSO and RBAC — can we enforce per-role access to logs and model keys?
[05:01] Dana Rivera: yes, RBAC is available; roles, SSO integration, and audit trails are standard. for Private you'll host keys in your KMS.
[05:08] Marco Ruiz: question about KV cache — is that exposed to customers to persist between sessions?
[05:13] Kofi Mensah: KV cache is managed by the runtime to speed up autoregressive calls; we also offer prefix caching and a persistent cache option for Dedicated/Private so you can persist warm state across sessions. hosted has cookie-like short-term caches but Dedicated gives more control.
[05:26] Aisha Patel: will need that for threaded conversations. also, can we do on-the-fly quantization to reduce cost?
[05:30] Kofi Mensah: we support quantized model variants — often pre-quantized at deployment time. on-the-fly quantization is tricky; it's usually part of the build/compile flow. Redwood Optimize gives recommendations for quantization per workload.
[05:42] Dana Rivera: quick check — are there any hard blockers from your side on compliance or network that would force Private?
[05:48] Olivia Chen: we prefer Private for EU-regulated customers, but for this initial pilot we could accept Dedicated in EU with customer-managed KMS. final decision pending legal.
[05:58] Marco Ruiz: timeline — we want a proof of concept in the next 4 weeks, and production in Q1 if results look good.
[06:04] Dana Rivera: OK that aligns; we'll prepare a 4-week pilot plan.
[06:08] Aisha Patel: in the POC we'd like to test 3 models: a smaller cheaper open model for baseline, a mid-sized long-context open model, and a higher-quality model variant for critical flows. can you recommend names?
[06:18] Kofi Mensah: yes — we typically test: 1) efficient open model (e.g., Mosaic-lite/agg), 2) long-context variant (LlamaX-long or equivalent), 3) high-quality 7B–13B variant tuned for multi-lingual. exact names vary as open ecosystem moves fast; we'll map to current validated models.
[06:34] Marco Ruiz: will we be able to measure hallucination rates?
[06:37] Kofi Mensah: yes, our evals include hallucination/error rate metrics tied to prompt sets. we'll instrument that in the POC.
[06:43] Dana Rivera: i'm going to recap and confirm next steps — Dana to send pricing and pilot plan, Kofi to run initial benchmarks and share the model catalog + 100k-context notes, Olivia to send compliance doc list, customer to confirm stakeholders and pilot datasets. anything to add?
[06:56] Olivia Chen: please include network diagram requirements for Dedicated/Private in the security pack.
[07:01] Dana Rivera: will do.
[07:03] Aisha Patel: one more quick thing — can you run a small demo of the function-calling flow during the POC? like ticket create and update.
[07:09] Kofi Mensah: yes, demo and scripted tests.
[07:11] Marco Ruiz: sounds good.
[07:12] Dana Rivera: awesome — thanks all. we'll follow up with the materials.

(autogenerated notes / imperfect segments below)
